seo.metaDescription: Build threshold categories with thresholds(): breaks, tones and labels, which edge holds a value on a break, and heatmapLevel for matching a legend to a Heatmap.

props.markdown: A threshold turns a number into a category: a page load of 3.1 s is "Needs improvement", a margin of 9% is "Critical". `thresholds()` builds those categories once, and the same result colors a `ZoneMeter`, counts a `Legend` and tones the dots of a `DotHistogram`, so a value gets the same color everywhere. `heatmapLevel()` does the matching job for a `Heatmap`.

`thresholds(breaks, tones, labels, options)` takes the ascending break values, a tone for each bin and a label for each bin. There is one more tone and one more label than there are breaks: two breaks make three bins. A spec that does not fit, or breaks that are not finite and strictly ascending, throws, because it is a mistake in the code rather than in the data.

props.code:
import { thresholds } from 'tally-charts'

// Largest contentful paint in seconds: 2 breaks, 3 bins.
const lcp = thresholds(
  [2.5, 4],
  ['gain', 'warn', 'loss'],
  ['Good', 'Needs improvement', 'Poor'],
)

lcp.indexOf(3.1) // 1
lcp.toneOf(3.1) // 'warn'
lcp.toneOf('n/a') // undefined
lcp.indexOf('n/a') // -1

props.markdown: The result carries the plain data and three helpers. `bins` lists the bins as `{ label, tone, min, max }`; the first starts at `-Infinity` and the last ends at `Infinity`. `indexOf(value)` is the index of the bin that holds a value, or `-1` for a value that is missing or not a number. `toneOf(value)` is the tone of that bin. `legend(values)` counts how many of the values fall into each bin and returns entries for a `Legend`.

props.text: Which bin holds a value on a break

props.markdown: The `inclusive` option decides what happens to a value that is exactly on a break. With `'lower'`, the default, a bin is `[min, max)`: the value belongs to the bin above the break. With `'upper'` a bin is `(min, max]`: the value belongs to the bin below it, which is how Core Web Vitals count their tiers.

Take an LCP of exactly 2.5 s against the breaks `[2.5, 4]`. With `inclusive: 'lower'` it is "Needs improvement", because 2.5 starts the second bin. With `inclusive: 'upper'` it is "Good", because 2.5 ends the first one. The same goes for 4 s: "Poor" with `'lower'`, "Needs improvement" with `'upper'`. Values that are not on a break fall in the same bin either way.

props.code:
const strict = thresholds([2.5, 4], tones, labels) // 'lower'
const vitals = thresholds([2.5, 4], tones, labels, { inclusive: 'upper' })

strict.toneOf(2.5) // 'warn' (Needs improvement)
vitals.toneOf(2.5) // 'gain' (Good)

props.markdown: Pass the result to `ZoneMeter` as `zones`: the track draws one zone per bin and the marker sits at the value, which the screen reader hears together with the label of its bin. `ZoneMeter` reads `inclusive` too, so a value on a break lands in the bin your `thresholds()` call says. Pass it to `DotHistogram` as `toneBy` to tone each dot by its bin, and give `Legend` the result of `legend(values)` with `shape="dot"` for the swatches and counts.

Both meters show the same value, 2.5 s. The first uses `inclusive: 'upper'` and reads "Good"; the second uses the default and reads "Needs improvement". The two loads of exactly 2.5 s in the histogram are toned and counted as Good. The `thresholds()` result has methods, so it can only be passed from a client component. A Server Component can give `ZoneMeter` the plain `{ bins, inclusive }` instead; see [Server Components](/docs/server-components).

A `Heatmap` bins its values by `breaks` and paints each cell with a sequential level from 1 to 5. Its own legend already matches. When you draw the legend yourself, with a standalone `Legend` somewhere else on the page, `heatmapLevel(value, breaks)` gives the level the heatmap would paint that value with, so the swatches use the same colors. It returns `0` for a missing or non-numeric value.

The breaks are cleaned the way `Heatmap` cleans them: sorted, deduplicated and cut to the first four, which make the five bins. Four bins use the levels 1, 2, 4 and 5, and fewer bins spread over the range with the ends pinned, so do not work the levels out by hand. Take one value from each bin, ask `heatmapLevel` for its level and set it as the `level` of a `Legend` item. These are plain numbers, so the call also works in a Server Component.
